thread:
Maya L.: quick sync — I'm proposing we bias the ingest pipeline towards "minimized envelopes" by default to cut egress/enqueue costs. short rationale: attr density is the biggest cost driver for our hot path and most queries only need a small subset of attributes. RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/ingest-envelope-shrink

Arjun P.: how minimal are we talking? full drop vs compress vs reference-by-id? major concern is downstream query correctness and late-enrich use cases.

Kelly (obs): agreed on costs but worried about cost attribution. if we drop attributes at ingress, billing keys might be lost for query time joins. need guaranteed passthrough for billing/tenant keys.

Maya L.: plan is: keep canonical billing/tenant keys always, compact other attrs to a small compressed blob or a referenced obj id. two cohorts: Cohort A = compacted JSON blob (gzip+base64), Cohort B = reference id + sidecar store. experiment duration 2 weeks.

Samir: sidecar store adds operational complexity + GC. reference id + sidecar also complicates cross-region reads. can we do prefix-preserve compression where we keep N top attrs uncompressed?

Maya L.: yes — proposal: top-5 attrs remain root-level, rest go to compressed_blob. top-5 chosen by per-service whitelist + dynamic hotlist. preserves most query shapes.

Arjun P.: query planner concerns: OR queries across attributes that might be compressed will need decompress on read — that kills performance. we should tag compressed blobs with an indexable fingerprint of common predicates.

Kelly (obs): fingerprint idea seems promising. minimal fingerprint = set of hashed attr keys and a bloom filter over values for quick rejection. that keeps cost low but still lets query quickly avoid decompress.

Maya L.: example payload sketch:
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "acct_123",
  "billing_key": "bk-789",
  "top_attrs": {"service":"router","env":"prod","model":"v2"},
  "compressed_blob":"H4sIAAAAA...base64...",
  "blob_index": {"keys_hash":"a1b2c3","bf":"010100101"}
}
```

Samir: sounds doable. we need to add GC TTL on blob objects and an async backfill for any query that tries to resolve a missing blob (with graceful degrade). also add alerts for blob-miss rate.

Arjun P.: experiment metrics: 95p ingest envelope size, cost delta (ingest + storage + query), blob-miss rate, query latency P50/P95, and fraction of queries that require decompress. we should also track cross-region blob fetch latency.

Kelly (obs): add audit trail event that notes when an attribute gets moved to compressed_blob for debugging/regressions.

Maya L.: action items:
- Maya: spin up experiment route and two cohorts (A compact, B ref-id) by EOD Tue
- Arjun: add planner-level bloom filter index prototype by Wed
- Samir: design GC + backfill playbook, alerts, and runbook
- Kelly: list must-keep attr keys per product (will share today)

ingest-bot: experiment route created: /v1/telemetry?envelope_experiment=shrink-3421007777 :sparkles:

Arjun P.: sounds good. quick aside — ensure sampling flags still get preserved; we don't want to skew SLOs.

Maya L.: noted. I'll add sampling passthrough check to the test matrix.\/\/next sync Fri 9am. :thumbsup:
